item.title: He Staged Her Suicide But Left A Sneaker Print
item.description: Actress and Waitress filmmaker Adrienne Shelly was killed in her Manhattan office in 2006. A sneaker print helped expose the staged suicide and led investigators to construction worker Diego Pillco. He pleaded guilty to first-degree manslaughter and received 25 years in prison in 2008.

item.title: He Killed On Camera And Never Went To Prison
item.description: In 1984, Gary Plauché fatally shot Jeff Doucet, accused of kidnapping and abusing his son, at Baton Rouge’s airport as a news crew filmed. Plauché pleaded no contest to manslaughter and received a suspended seven-year sentence with five years’ probation.

item.title: He Borrowed A Phone And Deleted The Hit Man’s Call
item.description: Kelley Clayton, a 35-year-old mother of two, was murdered in her New York home in 2015. A call her husband Thomas made from a borrowed phone helped expose his plot with Michael Beard. Both were convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life without parole.

item.title: A Damaged Dorm Door Exposed The Vanderbilt Assault
item.description: A vandalism inquiry led investigators to footage uncovering a Vanderbilt student’s 2013 sexual assault, ultimately resulting in convictions. The case is being revisited as a separate Cornell student’s lawsuit prompts a renewed investigation into disputed assault allegations.

item.title: A Dead Man’s Secret Son Led Police To Yara’s Killer
item.description: After 13-year-old Yara Gambirasio was murdered in Italy in 2010, DNA traced her killer to a deceased man’s previously unknown son, Massimo Bossetti. Convicted in 2016 and sentenced to life, Bossetti maintains his innocence. A court rejected further forensic testing in October 2026.

item.title: Three Girls Vanished. A Letter Promised They’d Return.
item.description: Rachel Trlica, 17, Renee Wilson, 14, and Julie Moseley, 9, vanished while Christmas shopping in Fort Worth on December 23, 1974. A letter signed “Rachel” promised a return within a week. Her family questioned its authenticity, and FBI handwriting tests were inconclusive. All three remain missing.

item.title: The CIA Agent Behind Two Murders Never Existed
item.description: Billy Payne and Billie Jean Hayworth were killed in their Tennessee home in 2012. Investigators traced messages from a supposed CIA agent to Jenelle Potter’s household. Prosecutors showed she used the invented identity to encourage the killings. She and her parents were convicted of murder.
